summary: The new rate-limit module contains a boundary bug: `canMakeRequest` uses `<=` instead of `<`, permitting one request beyond REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW and contradicting `remainingRequests`, which correctly reports 0 remaining at the same input. Changing the comparison to `used < REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW` makes the two helpers consistent and enforces the documented cap.

findings.title: Off-by-one in canMakeRequest allows one request past REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW
findings.explanation: `canMakeRequest` uses `used <= REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW`, which returns true when `used` already equals the cap. With REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW = 20, an account that has made 20 requests is still permitted to make another, so the effective limit is 21 requests per window rather than the documented 20. This also directly contradicts `remainingRequests` in the same file, which returns 0 for `used = 20` — the two exported helpers give opposite answers at the boundary, so behavior depends on which one a caller happens to use. The comparison should be `used < REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW`.
findings.failureScenario: An account has already made 20 requests in the current window. `remainingRequests(20)` returns 0, but `canMakeRequest(20)` returns true, so a caller gating on `canMakeRequest` admits a 21st request and the rate limit is exceeded by one request every window.
